brief_premise_refuted.premise_as_given: "`water` uniquely has an initTools '<x>.created' bridge but NO CommandEventBridge '<x>.create' case -- i.e. a bridge listening for an event NOTHING EMITS."
brief_premise_refuted.verdict: REFUTED. The bridge has a live emitter.
brief_premise_refuted.why_the_premise_looked_true: The search was NAME-shaped. There is indeed no `case 'water.create':` in the CEB -- because there is no `water.create` COMMAND to have a case for. The emitter lives inside `case 'pool.create':` (CommandEventBridge.ts:1871, the enclosing case for line 2051, established by `grep -n -E "case '[a-zA-Z.\-]+':" ... | awk '$1>1850 && $1<2200'`). Searching for the CAPABILITY (who emits `<x>.created`) finds it; searching for the NAME (`case 'water.create'`) cannot. This is the D2 distinction exactly: not ABSENT, and not even UNREACHABLE -- WIRED, on the parent's channel, by design.
brief_premise_refuted.consequence: Had this been actioned as written, the 'fix' would have been to delete a live render bridge (REMOVE) or to mint a `water.create` verb and CEB case (WIRE) -- and minting that verb is precisely the rival write path ADR-0124 s4 exists to forbid. The imagined gap's fix was strictly worse than the measured state.

what_dispatches_water.question: Brief s3 -- find what (if anything) dispatches water.*, by capability not name.
what_dispatches_water.direct_verbs: NONE, and that is the design. Prior-run probe b7Edge Q-C, through the real composition root: `water.create` THREW 'no handler registered for: water.create'; same for water.delete and water.update. Corroborated statically: the descriptor's buildHandlers returns [] (PluginRegistry.ts:337) and `grep -rn 'water\.(create|created|delete|deleted|update|updated)'` across apps/packages/plugins/tools returns no handler declaration -- only comments, the CEB emit, the initTools subscriber and tests.
what_dispatches_water.the_real_write_path: `pool.create` (plugins/pool). It declares affectedStores ['pool','wall','slab','water'] and mints the water record; PoolPlanToolHandler.ts:461 `waterId: createId('water')` is the user-gesture entry point.
the_render_path_end_to_end: 1. DISPATCH  -- pool.create (PoolPlanToolHandler, LANDSCAPE palette row, pool activator).
2. EMIT      -- CommandEventBridge.ts:2051, inside `case 'pool.create':`, iterating `_poolCommitted.get('water')` and skipping any record whose parentId is not this pool.
3. SUBSCRIBE -- apps/editor/src/engine/initTools.ts, section-tag §FT-WATER (§POOL95 · ADR-0124 §4 · L-9941): `runtime.events.on('water.created', ...)` driving WaterMeshBuilder.
4. UNDO LEG  -- the same section registers `registerWaterRenderSink({update, remove})` over the SAME builder instance, because performUndoRedo emits no bus events. One builder, two roads.
what_dispatches_water.justification: WIRE (add a CEB `water.create` case) requires a `water.create` command to bridge; minting one is explicitly ruled out by ADR-0124 §4 and by the descriptor's own comment as 'a second, rival way to produce a water body with no pool around it'. REMOVE (delete the §FT-WATER bridge) would delete the only thing that puts water on screen: CommandEventBridge.ts:2036-2043 records that the paragraph 'water has no typed event, no subscriber and no mesh builder anywhere in the tree' USED to print on every pool, and that §POOL95 landed all three together because 'any one alone leaves it true'. Both candidate actions regress a working path. The only defect present is DOCUMENTARY: C11 §11's bridge matrix has no water row (see c11_matrix_says), and the CEB's own case-label census is where a name-shaped reader goes wrong.
what_dispatches_water.cited_section_tag: §FT-WATER (§POOL95 · ADR-0124 §4 · L-9941) -- cited as a §-tag rather than a line number per the brief.

c11_matrix_says: NO ROW. C11 §11's bridge matrix (docs/02-decisions/contracts/C11-ELEMENT-CREATION-PIPELINE.md) carries 14 element rows (Wall, Slab, Curtain Wall, Ceiling, Roof, Column, Beam, Floor, Wall Opening, Stair, Handrail, Furniture, Lighting, Room) and its own preamble requires it to be 'updated whenever a bridge is added, removed, or repaired'. §FT-WATER added a bridge (§POOL95, L-9941) and the matrix was not updated. My measurement REFUTES THE MATRIX BY OMISSION -- and the omission is not cosmetic: the matrix is exactly the artefact a reader consults to answer 'does water have a bridge?', and it answers NO by silence while CommandEventBridge.ts:2051 answers YES.

findings.claim: The B7 brief's stated measurement -- that §FT-WATER is 'a bridge listening for an event NOTHING EMITS' -- is FALSE. CommandEventBridge.ts:2051 emits `water.created` from inside `case 'pool.create':`. The premise was reached by searching for the NAME (`case 'water.create'`) instead of the CAPABILITY (who emits `<x>.created`). Acting on it would have deleted a live render path, or minted the rival `water.create` verb ADR-0124 §4 forbids.

findings.claim: C11 §11's bridge matrix has no `water` row, although §POOL95 added the create bridge and the matrix's own preamble makes updating it mandatory when a bridge is added. The matrix therefore answers 'no bridge' by silence for a family that has one -- which is how the B7 premise above became plausible in the first place.

Water has no plan representation. Measured as an absence over the 13 PlanSymbolBuilder classes that DO exist, not asserted. This is the family's first failing link, and it is undeclared anywhere -- unlike the delete leg, which initTools §FT-WATER declares explicitly and mirror-debt.json carries as a named row.
